Hi Liam — sorry for the confusion. You're right, Calendly sometimes defaults to the scheduler's browser timezone when the link was created and it can flip around at DST boundaries. To be explicit:

- Slot I proposed (what I meant): 10:00 AM BST on Tue, Oct 19, 2027 = 09:00 UTC.
- My Calendly event may have shown as 10:00 AM in my local PST view when I created it, which is why your calendar shows 11:00 AM BST after the conversion.

I'll attach a manual .ics to this thread with the explicit UTC and Europe/London times so your calendar client will show the correct slot. If 10:00 AM BST doesn't work, here are two alternates in Europe/London time:
- Tue Oct 19, 09:00 BST (08:00 UTC)
- Tue Oct 19, 11:00 BST (10:00 UTC)

Please accept the attached invite if 10:00 BST is fine, or reply with which alternate you'd like. Apologies for the handoff friction — we want this to be seamless on your side.

Attachment: demo-invite.ics (text/calendar)
